question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative inverse of $4$ modulo $9,$ denoted ${4}^{-1},$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
4\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,9).
$$

Note that since $\text{gcd}(4,9)=1,$ an inverse element exists and is unique up to congruence modulo $9.$

Since the modulus $n=9$ is small, we can find the inverse $x$ by computing exponents of $4$ (modulo $9$) until we get a result of $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{2} & ≡4\cdot 4≡16≡9+7≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {4}^{3} & ≡4\cdot 7≡28≡3\cdot 9+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $4\cdot 7≡1\,(\text{mod}\,9).$ Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of $4$ modulo $9$ is $7.$
